test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He __ordered for four cups of tea__ and some snacks.

options.text: gave ordered for four cups of tea
order for four cups of tea
ordered four for cups of tea

solution:
The correct answer is **'****ordered four cups of tea'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence,** "He ordered for four cups of tea and some snacks",** contains unnecessary wording.
 
• when ordering items, you typically use the verb "**order**" followed directly by the item being ordered. 
 
• The phrase "**for four cups of tea**" is redundant and not grammatically correct.
 
• From the above explanation it is clear that the correct phrase is **"ordered four cups of tea"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**, "**gave ordered for four cups of tea**," is incorrect because "gave" does not fit the context of the sentence. Additionally, "**ordered for**" is still incorrect usage.
 
• **Option 2**, "**order for four cups of tea**," is grammatically incorrect. It lacks the appropriate verb tense ("**ordered" instead of "order"**) and still contains the unnecessary "**for**."
 
• **Option 3**, "**ordered four for cups of tea**," is incorrect because the word order is misplaced. It should be "**ordered four cups of tea.**"
